correctness.rationale: For a vertex outside \(S\), having an outside neighbor is equivalent to the complement meeting another part, so restraint is exactly \(c(S)\ge2\). Domination is automatic if \(S\) meets at least two parts, while one-part support dominates exactly when it is the whole part. Inclusion-exclusion over sets meeting at most one part and complements meeting at most one part gives the stated formulas, and the minimum/count cases follow immediately. I independently replayed the definition against the criterion on representative multipartite profiles, including \((1,1)\), \((1,2)\), \((2,2)\), \((1,1,1)\), \((1,2,3)\), and \((2,2,2)\); the inspected verifier exhausts all isomorphism types through order ten.

value.rationale: Although the full polynomial is apparently unpublished, the classification on a complete multipartite graph follows immediately from two definition-level observations: an outside vertex sees exactly the other parts, and a selected one-part set dominates only when it is the full part. The formulas are then routine inclusion-exclusion. Under the same value bar used for other complete-multipartite domination variants, this is a clean expository specialization rather than a substantive new structural gap.

final_claim: For every connected complete multipartite graph, a proper set is restrained dominating exactly when its complement meets at least two parts and the set itself either meets at least two parts or equals one entire part; the two closed size-enumerator formulas and the stated minimum values and counts follow.
limitations: The all-set formulas appear absent from the checked literature, but the classification is a direct definition-level specialization of multipartite adjacency.
